summary: Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University, where he is attested from 1995 to 2002.

Koken Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Rissho University from circa 1950 to 1960. He taught Guohui Shi and spent his career at Rissho University as assistant professor, department chair, director, professor, and emeritus professor.
Koki Kawagishi was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1976, he is attested as holding professorships at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University.

Komal Asrani is a scholar in computational studies and Indology. Asrani studied at Government Engineering College, earned a Ph.D. at Uttar Pradesh Rajarshi Tandon Open University (2002–2005), and held a computer science post at Babu Banarasi Das Group in 2006.
Konchok Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held an attested post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.
Konchok Zangpo was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Konrad Gottlob Anton was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1763 to 1767. In 1775, he became Professor of Oriental and Classical Languages at the University of Wittenberg.
Konrad Ihlefeld was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Rostock in 1858. He served as director of Porayar Seminary from 1878 to 1885.

Konrad Klaus is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Göttingen and Marburg under Wilhelm Rau and Michael Hahn. He held temporary professorships at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn (1999–2001), and succeeded Claus Vogel at Bonn in 2001.
Konrad Meisig is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ulrich Schneider from circa 1980 to 1986. He held a post at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1999 to 2019.

Kosaku Hamada was an archaeologist, sinologist, and japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (1902–1905). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1909–1913) and Kyoto University (~1913–1938), and taught Seiichi Mizuno.

Kosei Ishii is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa. He held posts at Waseda, served as assistant professor at Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and was a Buddhist studies professor at Komazawa University (2006–2021).

Kosei Tada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1957 to 1961. He held a post at Taisho University and served as board chairman of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies (attested 2004).
Koshin Suzuki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He also held a researcher post at Taisho University, attested between 1995 and 1998.

Koshiro Tamaki was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo University, University of Tokyo (1964–1976), Tohoku University (~1976–1979), and Nihon University (1979–1986).

Kosho Kawamura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He held posts at Toyo University (~1954–1995), Minobusan University, and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Kosho Mizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku and Bukkyo Universities. He served as assistant professor (~1961) and president (~1975–1989) of Bukkyo University, and headed Tokai Gakuen (~1994–2011) and Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen (~1999–2014).

Kosho Uchiyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda University and under Kodo Sawaki. He taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (1937–1940), succeeded Sawaki in 1965, and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).

Koshu Itabashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy and Sendai Daiichi High School. He graduated from Tohoku University, where he studied from circa 1949 to 1953 under Teruji Ishizu.
